verdict.rationale: Galileo's own docs show it captures LLM-call traces. Instrumentation records every session, trace and span, the Python SDK offers an `@log` decorator for spans, and OpenTelemetry-based distributed tracing joins spans into a single trace, with a quickstart for logging a first trace. However, the pack never says which fields a trace records; only a Cost alert metric hints at usage data. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that traces capture inputs and outputs, latency/duration per call, and token usage counts, plus independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: Once instrumented, Galileo captures every session, trace, and span, producing a structured stream of real-time data.
You can also use the `@log` decorator to log spans.
Galileo joins all spans that share a trace ID into a single trace.
Learn how to log your first trace with Galileo
